scope: Private WordPress only; production Pages, original branding, daily-source code, backend cutover and paid plans unchanged.
change: Runtime-owned single-entry metadata cache checks site root and complete pointer, clones/freezes validated manifests, skips entries above 256 KiB, and remembers a new manifest only after R2 persistence. The runtime cache also compares the complete pointer. Full content/media/theme reconciliation, snapshot integrity and coordinator leases/commits are retained.

localValidation.generatedLoaderWarnings: Existing direct-eval and duplicate-object-key warnings retained; loader unchanged
localValidation.scope: Runtime-owned metadata cache, one entry; no payload bytes or request state cached

limits: Small sequential samples; no randomized order or statistical speedup claim.
Remote phase clocks advance on I/O; phase durations are not isolated CPU/operation cost.
Timing includes complete native response and, for content mutations, a small local ownership-guard file write.

final.scope: Complete backup after runtime manifest cache baseline/candidate and cold readback verification and owned cleanup; all original content, historical revisions, media and metadata retained; owned draft/revisions absent

backup.scope: Authenticated remote R2 backup; every decoded entry verified; restore is a separate acceptance

observation.scope: Finite native HTTP experiment, not browser UI or long-term free-tier acceptance; events are not unique requests and sampled heap/files are not whole-isolate memory.

limits: A metadata cache deliberately does not detect an out-of-band overwrite/deletion of the same revision key while the runtime remains warm. Application revisions use unique keys; fresh cold boot, operator checks and backup validation still read R2 directly.
One entry has a 256 KiB serialized UTF-8 cap; this is not a bound on total JavaScript heap or transient serialization allocations. Initial metadata was 72,949 bytes.

Ten baseline and ten candidate requests are sequential, not randomized. Baseline measured requests were warm; candidate includes two cold requests. Do not infer a stable speedup from mixed distributions.
No browser/UI repeat or new independent empty-environment restore in this cycle. Previous canceled UI events remain unexplained.
Cold starts, save/lock latency, more native workflows, practical handoff, real-device input and sustained free-tier capacity remain open.
Snapshot storage accumulates with revisions. Current account cost/usage and retention require a separate owning-source check; fewer reads do not establish zero future cost.
